headline: Visa's CEO says trust is the biggest barrier to scale
body: Visa's credential base reached 5.2 billion at the end of its fiscal fourth quarter, up 6%. On the earnings call on Oct. 27, CEO Ryan McInerney said "in agentic, trust is the biggest barrier to scale", and Visa expects its nearly 50 AI partners in production to double in the coming months.
note: Visa's own framing puts identity and spending authority at the center of agent purchases, which are the checks banks and card issuers will also need to build into their agent products.

figure.label: Visa credentials at the end of fiscal Q4, up 6%

evidence.text: Visa expects its roster of nearly 50 artificial intelligence partners in production to double in the coming months, as it prepares to handle purchases that consumers and businesses delegate to software.

During Visa’s fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on Tuesday (Oct. 27) after the markets closed, CEO Ryan McInerney described the work required to identify an agent, connect it to a customer and confirm that its spending follows the customer’s instructions.
“It is clear that in agentic, trust is the biggest barrier to scale,” he told analysts.
Visa’s credential base reached 5.2 billion at the end of the fiscal fourth quarter, up 6%, as management described expansion through co-branded cards, affluent products and debit portfolios.
